description: A single-panel DTA (differential thermal analysis) thermogram of the 35 h milled powder of a Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 high entropy steel, recorded from 200 °C to 1000 °C (x-axis "Temperature (°C)", labelled ticks at 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, 1000). The y-axis is labelled "Heat Flow (µV/mg)" but carries no printed numeric tick values, so event magnitudes cannot be quantified from the panel. A downward-pointing arrow labelled "Exothermic" in the top-left corner fixes the sign convention: exothermic events appear as downward deflections. The blue trace is essentially flat except for two downward deflections marked by dotted vertical lines and labelled "420°C" and "520°C": a shallow, comparatively broad dip at 420 °C and a deeper, sharper dip at 520 °C; minor baseline undulations occur near 350-400 °C and 750-900 °C. The figure demonstrates that the as-milled powder undergoes two exothermic reactions on continuous heating, at ~420 °C and ~520 °C, which the citing text assigns to γ-brass-type ordering/texturing and to Fe3Si-type intermetallic formation, respectively, and which motivated the ex-situ annealing/XRD study in Fig. 5.

subfigures.description: Single-panel DTA thermogram, x-axis Temperature (°C) from 200 to 1000, y-axis Heat Flow (µV/mg) without numeric ticks; downward 'Exothermic' arrow; two dotted markers labelled 420°C and 520°C on two downward (exothermic) deflections, the 520 °C dip being the deeper of the two.

observations.observation: The figure is a single DTA curve with x-axis 'Temperature (°C)' spanning 200 to 1000 with ticks every 100 °C.
The y-axis is labelled 'Heat Flow (µV/mg)' but no numeric tick values are printed, so the magnitudes of the thermal events are not quantifiable from the panel.
A downward-pointing arrow labelled 'Exothermic' in the upper-left corner indicates exothermic events are plotted as downward deflections.
Two dotted vertical lines annotate the trace at '420°C' and '520°C', each coinciding with a downward (exothermic) dip.
The 520 °C deflection is visibly deeper and narrower than the shallow, broader 420 °C deflection; the trace is otherwise near-flat with small undulations.
The caption states the figure is a DTA thermogram of the 35 h milled powder of the high entropy steel, measured from 200 °C to 1000 °C.
The citing text states the DTA reveals exothermic events at 420 °C (693 K) and 520 °C (793 K).
The ~420 °C exothermic event is attributed in the citing text to ordering and/or texturing of the γ-brass type phase (linked to Fig. 5(d)).
The ~520 °C exothermic event is attributed in the citing text to the formation of an Fe3Si-type phase (linked to Fig. 5(e)).
The citing text states the 35 h milled powder is thermally stable up to 500 °C, with the Fe3Si-type intermetallic phase (hP16) evolving at 600 °C and growing up to 800 °C.
Annealing temperatures of 400 °C, 500 °C, 600 °C and 800 °C were chosen on the basis of this DTA result for ex-situ XRD analysis.
